audience_note: This record concerns the city struck by the first atomic bomb used in war and its preserved ruin. It refers to mass death and injury, and casualty detail is left to the event record.
author: historian-agent:m-6
title: Hiroshima and the Genbaku Dome
summary: Hiroshima began in 1589 when Mori Terumoto started a castle on the Ota river delta, and it became a city in 1889. On 6 August 1945 the first atomic bomb used in war exploded over it. The ruined former Industrial Promotion Hall, the Genbaku Dome, was preserved as a peace memorial.

uncertainty.note: Start is the year Mori Terumoto began the castle (1589); the city page says it was tentatively completed in 1591. End is the present.

as_recorded.value: In 1589, Terumoto Mori began construction of a castle on a delta
Hiroshima officially became one of the first cities in all of Japan in April 1, 1889

importance.justification: The first city hit by an atomic bomb in war; the Genbaku Dome is a UNESCO World Heritage property and a global symbol of peace.

phases.description: Built by Hiroshima Prefecture to a design by Jan Letzel; work began 1914 and it opened in 1915.
Stood as the Prefectural Commercial Exhibition Hall, later the Industrial Promotion Hall.
Left as strongly damaged ruins near the hypocentre after the bombing of 6 August 1945.
City council resolved in 1966 to preserve it; preservation projects in 1967 and 1989 stabilised the ruin, kept as it was just after the bombing.

materials.material: brick with partial steel reinforcement; exterior of stone and mortar

reviewer_note: Shape domed_building. The record is the city, but the pin and model are the Genbaku Dome (UNESCO point) because the model rules need one structure; the city centre lies about 1.1 km away. Least sure of the dome diameter: 10.6 m is the long axis of a pseudo-ellipse from a 1989 university paper, short axis 8.6 m.
